push_notification_opt_in.note: QA-20260823-04 VERIFIED+CLOSED this run (PR #66, staging bef67c5, CI green: changes/test/deploy-staging/e2e all pass). The filed finding was stale copy; the real defect was larger and is what got fixed -- every remaining push category is office-only since bd58fa0, and getPushConfigAction filters categories by role, so a crew tap on Enable spent the browser's one-shot permission prompt for an empty 'What you receive' list and zero notifications, forever, silently (a denied prompt is close to unrecoverable, so it was pure downside against any future real crew push). NotificationsRow now renders null when pushCategoriesForRole(role) is empty and carries no hardcoded promise of its own; NotificationsSetup already states accurate copy per state. Live-proven BOTH ways on deployed staging with throwaway logins: crew /my-jobs shows the 'Your device' section intact (quick sign-in + user manual present) with 0 matches for the opt-in row, the old row text, or /put on a job/i; an admin on the SAME page still sees the row and it expands -- so the gate reads the category registry rather than blanket-removing the panel. business_settings.push_enabled=false (master kill switch, pre-existing, unrelated) means the category list itself still could not be observed -- recorded rather than glossed; it does not touch what was under test, since the gate is computed from role before any config fetch. New permanent spec e2e/crew/push-optin.spec.ts guards the wiring; the unit guard (adding crew to any audience fails the test) guards the cause. Cleanup verified zero in one pass (events_log/staff/profiles/auth.users), delete errors surfaced not swallowed.

website_lead_ingest.note: FRESH CODE (e30fb02 direct website lead ingest /api/ingest/lead + migration 0102). No finding — freshest code verified correct. HAPPY-PATH HTTP e2e not reachable: LEAD_INGEST_SECRET not in this env by design, so an authenticated POST cannot be driven; auth-boundary and dedup/immutability proven by other means above. SPEC GAP: /api/ingest/lead has no permanent e2e spec — an auth-boundary spec (401/405) is writable without the secret but the e2e 'public' project depends on the setup auth project, which needs E2E_* creds absent from this env, so no spec could be validated locally and none shipped (AUDIT: a spec must pass locally first).
